title: Riverbend Patient Payment Plan Re-age and Reinstatement Limits
content:
A **Patient Payment Plan** tier sets how often a past-due plan may be re-aged, how many installments (the down payment excluded) must have been paid before a re-age, how a re-age treats the missed amount, the calendar days after the default date within which a defaulted plan may be reinstated, the percent of the missed installment amount that must be paid to reinstate, and the number of reinstatements allowed over the plan's life.

| Tier | Re-ages over the plan's life | Installments paid before a re-age | Reinstatement window (calendar days) | Catch-up (percent of missed amount) | Reinstatements over the plan's life |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Riverbend Short-Term Payment Plan | 1 | 1 | 30 | 100 | 0 |
| Riverbend Standard Payment Plan | 1 | 2 | 30 | 100 | 1 |
| Riverbend Extended Payment Plan | 1 | 3 | 45 | 100 | 1 |
| Riverbend Long-Term Payment Plan | 2 | 3 | 60 | 100 | 1 |
| Riverbend Assistance-Linked Payment Plan | 2 | 1 | 60 | 50 | 2 |
| Riverbend Hardship Payment Plan | 2 | 1 | 90 | 50 | 2 |

**Re-age method (all tiers):** the missed amount is moved to the end of the term.

## Hypothetical illustration

A defaulted plan with 2 missed installments of 100.00 has a missed amount of 200.00. At a 100 percent catch-up the payment to reinstate is 200.00; at a 50 percent catch-up it is 100.00. On the Short-Term tier no reinstatement is available at all, since the tier allows 0 reinstatements.
